name: Cassie
notes: Bad Boy / NextSelection, produced end-to-end by Ryan Leslie: minimal drum-machine R&B, 2006–2009. The research gives "94–112 straight (backbeat 2&4)" with six sourced tempos, so the mode sits at 100. The drum claim is stated as a superlative and the model is built to it: "the defining parameter is subtraction — a single dry kick on 1 and the 8th before 3, a hard clap/snare flat on 2&4, one 16th hat pair per bar, and no fills; the pattern never varies across a record." So the kick is exactly two hits with `syncopation` 0.02, the hat lane sits at 0.04 fill density, `fills` are pushed to every sixteen bars, `quantizeStrength` is 0.96 and `velocityVar` is 0.08 — the tightest, quietest, sparsest kit in this whole section, and the direct opposite of the parent genre's under-quantised swung 16ths. Harmony is "two-chord minor shuttles with a thin bell or square-wave riff, everything played by Leslie himself", so the triad share is 0.56 and the voicing sits high and close. "Cassie's near-whispered, pitch-limited alto is doubled rather than harmonised, with a 3–4 pitch hook" is a twelve-semitone melody register — the narrowest here — a 0.9 step share, a 3–4 pitch motif and a counter density of 0.26. "A short-decay synth-bass note on the root under the clap, no slides, no sustain; the low end is almost absent by design" is `mirror_kick` at a 0.92 root follow with `glideProb` 0; there is no `bass808` block. "No bridge, cold end" is why `switchUpProb` is 0.01. ⚠ Every velocity and density number is INFERRED; the research evidences the minimalism by the catalogue's consistency rather than by numbers. ⚠ `session.keys` is INFERRED: the entry's Keys line gives "minor-mode two-chord vamps [LOW-CONF]" and enumerates no tonic, so the values here and their weights are this author's reading of that line. ⚠ **`chords.harmonicRhythm` re-weighted (2026-08-17, harmony variety floor).** The entry's harmony line is "minor-mode two-chord vamps" / "two-chord minor shuttles with a thin bell or square-wave riff", and the engine's `vamp` value is *one* chord held for the whole clip (`generators::chords`: "One chord for the whole pattern") — so weighting `vamp` at the top rendered a **one**-chord bed the research nowhere describes. The chord motion the entry states is now carried by `1_per_bar` (the pair over a 2-bar cell) and `2_bars_per_chord` (the pair over a 4-bar cell), with `vamp` kept as the minority for the held reading. ⚠ The split between those two rates is **INFERRED** — the entry names the device, not its rate. ⚠ **`cellShapes: [["1"]]` was authored dead and it was costing this model the bassline variety floor.** A one-degree cell of the root says exactly what `followRootsProb` says, and because `bass.rs` prefers a cell over `passingTones` it made `followRootsProb` unreadable — every note was the root at every seed, so the only thing that moved was the engine's octave choice. Measured: **367 distinct basslines in 1,000 seeds** against `bass.rs`'s floor of 500. The rhythm stays `mirror_kick` for the research's *"short-decay synth-bass note on the root under the clap, no slides, no sustain"*, and `glideProb` stays 0 for the same line. ⚠ **INFERRED:** `followRootsProb` 0.92, the `M2` beside `P5`, and `anticipationProb` 0.20 are lane-conventional, not sourced — the research gives the bass a level and a decay but no movement rate. They are the smallest set that reaches a producer's 500 basslines, and 92% of notes are still the root. ⛔ The bassline declares `loopVerbatim`: the entry says "a short-decay synth-bass note on the root under the clap, no slides, no sustain; the low end is almost absent by design", so this low end is static by description rather than thin by accident. `engine/tests/bass.rs::static_low_end` waives the saturation share for it and nothing else — the absolute floor of 500 distinct basslines still applies and this model clears it. The declaration needs the corroborating `followRootsProb` of 0.92 beside it, so the word alone could not buy the exemption.
